claims.text: The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has a uniform structure without significant pre-existing phase segregation.
Increasing temperature from room or moderate temperature into the high-temperature operating regime activates dynamic recovery.
Elevated temperature enhances dislocation mobility in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Elevated temperature enhances atomic diffusion in the coating.
Enhanced diffusion and dislocation movement increase dislocation annihilation and rearrangement.
Dynamic recovery redistributes microscopic plastic deformation during sliding.
Dynamic recovery makes microscopic deformation more spatially homogeneous.
More homogeneous deformation reduces localized stress concentrations.
Reduced deformation localization and stress concentration improve overall wear resistance.
High-temperature friction simulations will produce a lower wear volume than baseline-temperature simulations.
High-temperature friction simulations will produce a more homogeneous microscopic deformation pattern than baseline-temperature simulations.
High-temperature simulations will show lower local peaks in dislocation density.
Thermal softening occurs at elevated temperature even while localized wear is predicted to decrease.
At room or moderate temperature, dislocation activity is less dynamic and deformation is more localized.
The baseline condition has higher wear than the proposed high-temperature condition.
The predicted improvements apply only below the onset of catastrophic phase transformation or coating degradation.
The controlled intervention is an increase from a room- or moderate-temperature baseline to a designated high-temperature condition.
